sarah: Heads up — node gpu-n1 (rack r3) started spitting Xid errors again during a 12:30 job run. Quick paste of the dmesg tail I grabbed:

sarah: ```
[ 1203.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00:00): 31, pid=2345, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1203.456910] NVRM: GPU at 0000:af:00:00 has fallen off the bus.
[ 1203.457012] kernel: nvme0n1: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[ 1204.800123] nvidia: ECC corrected error on GPU 0: 4 (32-bit), total 102
[ 1205.001234] audit: type=1701 audit(161000): auid=1000 pid=2345 comm="python"
```

sarah: I also grabbed a quick `journalctl -k` snippet and an `nvidia-smi -q` snapshot, putting both below.

ajay: can you paste the `nvidia-smi` short output? want to see ECC counters and processes. also which kernel version?

sarah: nvidia-smi snippet: ```
Timestamp                           : 2024-05-03T12:30:03
Driver Version                      : 525.89.02
Attached GPUs                       : 1
GPU 0000:af:00.0
    Product Name                    : A100-SXM4-80GB
    ECC Mode                       : Enabled
    ECC Errors (Volatile)          : 4 (corrected), 0 (uncorrected)
    Processes                       :
        PID 2345  CGroup: /kubepods/...  python (model-worker)
```

sarah: kernel: `5.15.0-80-generic`

ben: ok — this looks like recurring corrected ECC + an Xid 31 (GPU fell off the bus). Two quick operational things: 1) capture the tail of kernel/dmesg + the nv-smi snapshot at the moment of the Xid, 2) attach PCI topology + last-looking-cgroup info so we can attribute to the pod/VM.

ben: one-liner I use to grab a compact artifact after an Xid: ```
# collect last 200 kernel lines with relevant keywords and nv-smi snapshot
journalctl -k -b -n 2000 | rg "NVRM: Xid|ECC corrected|GPU has fallen" -n > /tmp/xid-kernel.log
nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).xml
iptables-save > /tmp/iptables-$(date +%s).txt  # in case networking induced resets
tar -czf /tmp/gpu-artifact-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).tgz /tmp/xid-kernel.log /tmp/nvidia-smi-*.xml /var/log/kern.log || true
# upload to ops collection endpoint (internal)
curl -sS -F file=@/tmp/gpu-artifact-*.tgz https://ops-upload.internal.redwood/api/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```

ben: put that behind a tiny systemd timer or a k8s sidecar so we don't miss the window. also gzip the dmesg instead of full journalctl to keep size down.

lina: for parsing rules, suggest we extract these fields into the envelope: `node`, `timestamp`, `gpu_id`, `xid_code`, `ecc_corrected_count`, `pid`, `cmdline`, `cgroup`, `driver_version`, `kernel_version`, `dmesg_snippet`.

lina: regex we used in the parser: ```
// sample PCRE to capture Xid
/NVRM: Xid \(PCI:(?<pci>[^)]+)\): (?<xid>\d+), pid=(?<pid>\d+), (?<msg>.*)/
/ECC corrected error on GPU (?<gpu>\d+): (?<count>\d+)/
```

ajay: can we also grab the KV cache size and recent inference sequence length? sometimes large sequences + small KV cache kernels trigger hangs. `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` shows memory pressure but not KV cache; we should add agent-level telemetry from the model runtime (prefix length, kv-cache-usage) into the envelope.

sarah: noted — our model-worker already exposes `/metrics` with `kv_cache_bytes` and `active_sequence_len`. i'll add a hook to call it when an Xid is detected and include in the artifact.

oncall-bot: autopruner: node gpu-n1 flagged for drain (reason: recurring Xid 31 + ECC corrected spikes). ticket OP-4821 created and assigned to sarah. :construction:

sarah: thanks — i'm going to cordon/drain and swap the card. i'll also run the artifact collection and drop the tarball link into the ticket.

ben: one more ops note: we should keep a rolling 8MB ring buffer of recent dmesg lines per node and a tiny FIFO of `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots (last 5) so the parser doesn't have to request full journalctl on-demand. that made triage 3x faster in our last run.

lina: agreed — i'll open a PR for the ring buffer agent. schema: compressed gz chunks with metadata JSON (node/gpu/ts) and a small index. we can add retention policy 7 days by default.

sarah: perfect. i'll update the runbook with the commands above and link the parser PR once it's live. :thumbsup:
